g1-e.texto: Do you open 4 or more sessions at once, struggle to know where each one is and, when an idea comes up in the middle of something, put it in any of them and end up not knowing what comes next?

g2-e.texto: Do you send a message to the model and realize, 3 seconds later, that you left something out or got something wrong?

g3-e.texto: Do you come back from a break not knowing where you were or what’s next, and in every new session explain everything to the model again?

g4-e.texto: Do long answers tire you out, do you lose track of what you already read, and does the model ask you to reread documentation you already reviewed?

g5-e.texto: Do your tokens go on sessions that reread the same things, does your context get polluted every time you change a decision, and you don’t know what the model remembers?

g6-e.texto: Did your internet go down and your work with AI stopped?

g7-e.texto: Does writing down everything you think tire you, and your messages to the model come out half-done?

s1-p1.texto: If you sent it and something was missing,

s1-p2.texto: you send another and another to correct it,

s1-1.texto: With STL, your notes go to an Inbox first:

s1-2.texto: they wait there, and you can review and edit them as much as you want

s1-3.texto: before the director actually sends them to the model

s1-c.texto: Goodbye to fixing half-finished messages: you check it before it goes.

s2-p1.texto: With four or more sessions at once,

s2-p3.texto: and you wear yourself out trying to follow them all

s2-1.texto: With STL, everything comes in through a single channel

s2-4.texto: on the next strategic step, one at a time

s2-c.texto: Free from juggling sessions: your attention, on a single step.

s3-p1.texto: When ideas or tweaks come up in the middle of something,

s3-p2.texto: the rest falls behind and gets lost

s3-1.texto: With STL, your idea goes to the Inbox,

s3-2.texto: the director gives it its place on the route

s3-3.texto: and, if doing it now is not strategic, it waits in its phase.

s3-4.texto: So you finish what you were going to do first,

s3-5.texto: without losing that new idea or tweak,

s3-6.texto: and it stays on the route where it belongs

s3-c.texto: No idea gets lost, and you finish what you started.

s4-p1.texto: Reading three pages of an answer in a row wears you out,

s4-p3.texto: You end up not reading what the model answers

s4-1.texto: STL shows you one idea at a time,

s4-2.texto: with a «Got it» button before uncovering the next.

s4-3.texto: What comes next waits covered until you get there.

s4-4.texto: It can also read it aloud to you,

s4-5.texto: and you can comment on each idea or paragraph

s4-6.texto: without explaining to the model which part you mean

s4-c.texto: Reading no longer wears you out: one idea at a time.

s5-p1.texto: How do you know what you already read and what you didn't?

s5-1.texto: With STL, each idea you read stays marked

s5-2.texto: and you know exactly where you are:

s5-3.texto: what you have read and what you haven't

s5-c.texto: You always know where you are.

s6-p1.texto: Does the model change documents and ask you to reread them?

s6-1.texto: With STL, what you already read stays sealed;

s6-2.texto: what is new arrives separately, in a short document,

s6-3.texto: with only what changed, and easy to read

s6-c.texto: Never reread what you already read.

s7-p1.texto: Does the model ask you something you already decided?

s7-1.texto: STL has its own project memory system:

s7-3.texto: and, before asking you, the director searches.

s7-4.texto: It was already decided: option A.

s8-p1.texto: Each new session rereads the same things,

s8-1.texto: With STL, the director receives everything together, with the map,

s8-c.texto: Your tokens, only for what is new.

s9-p1.texto: Do you come back from a break

s9-p2.texto: and not know where you were or what's next in each session?

s9-1.texto: With STL, the «Where we left off» section is waiting for you:

s9-2.texto: an always up-to-date report of what was done

s9-3.texto: and of where the project stands,

s9-4.texto: with a single next mission in view:

s9-5.texto: you just pick up, and you already know what's next

s9-c.texto: You pick up right where you left off.

s11-p1.texto: In every new session, do you explain everything to it again

s11-p2.texto: to define what it will be about?

s11-1.texto: STL builds its own optimized system

s11-3.texto: the state stays in files, in your project map

s11-5.texto: The director already knows it all: you need to repeat nothing

s11-c.texto: No more repeating yourself to the model.

s12-1.texto: With STL, a decision you change is marked replaced in the history

s12-2.texto: and is no longer part of the new context that goes to the model:

s12-3.texto: you only send decisions you approved

s12-c.texto: A clean context, with only what you approved.

s13-p1.texto: The model is a black box:

s13-p2.texto: sometimes you don't know what it remembers, what it doesn't, and why

s13-1.texto: STL shows you, graphically, the whole inference cycle:

s13-2.texto: how your team and the model communicate,

s13-3.texto: how long each one takes to carry out its parts, and its usage,

s13-4.texto: and exactly who asks what of whom.

s13-5.texto: So you understand what happens each time you ask the model something

s13-6.texto: and you keep this history, to audit it and learn

s13-c.texto: The black box, now in plain sight.

s14-p1.texto: Your internet goes down in the middle of your work,

s14-p2.texto: and the chat with the model stops: now what?

s14-1.texto: With STL Studio, you keep working offline:

s14-2.texto: the Inbox collects your notes, tweaks and deliveries,

s14-3.texto: and you keep reading documents and answers

s14-5.texto: Nothing is lost: everything stays in the project memory.

s14-6.texto: When the connection comes back, the director receives it all together.

s14-c.texto: No internet, and your work goes on.

s15-p1.texto: You have the idea clear in your head,

s15-p2.texto: but writing it all out is tiring,

s15-p3.texto: and only half of it reaches the model.

s15-1.texto: With STL, you dictate it: you talk as you would with a friend,

s15-2.texto: naturally, explaining what you have in mind.

s15-3.texto: You can even ramble, it doesn't matter: the director will understand you.

s15-4.texto: What matters is that you express your idea the way you really want it,

s15-5.texto: in your natural language: leave the understanding to the director.

s15-6.texto: Your note is transcribed on your computer.

s15-7.texto: Since it goes to the Inbox and not straight to the model,

s15-8.texto: you read it and correct it before it arrives:

s15-9.texto: you take out or add whatever you want.

s15-c.texto: Talk, correct and send: no extra typing.

como-1.texto: Want to try the Studio now? This is how you start.

como-2.texto: First, bring it to your computer: clone the repository, or download it from GitHub.

como-3.texto: Put it in the folder where you want to work.

como-4.texto: For your peace of mind, first ask your model for a security scan: to confirm it brings nothing malicious.

como-5.texto: Then ask it to install it.

como-6.texto: From there, the Studio guides you step by step.

como-7.texto: If you have any doubt, read the documentation.

como-c.texto: Done: you are up and running.
